# clio backup restore

Replace the selected store with the archive (never a merge); a pre-restore snapshot is taken first unless --no-pre-backup; for a SQLite store the swap removes the target's write-ahead log before it renames the new store in, so a crash in that window loses whatever that log had not yet written; a Postgres restore replaces the target in one transaction and has no such window; --no-pre-backup is what leaves that window with no way back. Exit codes: 0 clean restore, 1 operational failure, 2 refused, 3 partial or not-durable restore, 75 means the command could not report a clean success and that nothing was lost or invalid, and the command's own message says whether a retry helps: a storage lock conflict is cleared by retrying, and a restore that left a derived difference is not. Here that code is a restore that loaded every user-data row and differs in a table the store rebuilds; retrying it reloads the same archive and reproduces the same count, and the index pipeline reconciles it on its next pass

## Usage

```
clio backup restore ID | clio backup restore --latest [--yes] [--no-input] [--no-pre-backup] [--allow-missing-keys] [--dry-run] [--output json|text]
```

## Description

replaces the selected store with the archive's, never a merge: the archive's database and key store overwrite the live ones, a SQLite restore swaps the archived database file in, and a Postgres restore replaces every row of the target in one transaction, so a failure halfway leaves the target untouched. A pre-restore snapshot of the current store is taken first by default; --no-pre-backup skips it and says so. The swap of a SQLite store clears the target's write-ahead log before it renames the new store in, so a crash in that window loses whatever the log had not yet written into the store; a Postgres restore replaces the target in one transaction and has no such window; that snapshot is the only thing that covers it, so --no-pre-backup accepts the window rather than removing it. The archive holds key material when it carries a key member, so keep it owner-only; --allow-missing-keys accepts an archive without one and the restored content is then permanently unreadable. On a terminal the snapshot id must be typed exactly; off one, --yes is required, and --no-input forces the non-interactive path

## Arguments

| Argument | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ID` | yes | Snapshot id from the backup directory's listing; `restore` restores that archive and `verify` re-checks it. |

## Options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--latest` |  |  | Selects the newest snapshot instead of a positional id; `backup_cli::resolve_restore_id` resolves it. |
| `--yes` |  |  | Answers the confirmation gate in `backup_restore_cli::confirm`, restoring without a typed snapshot id. |
| `--no-input` |  |  | Forces the non-interactive path in `backup_restore_cli::confirm`, refusing rather than prompting. |
| `--no-pre-backup` |  |  | Skips the pre-restore snapshot the restore backends take by default; that snapshot is the only way back. |
| `--allow-missing-keys` |  |  | Accepts an archive with no key member; `backup_restore_refusals::refuse_missing_keys` then restores content that stays permanently unreadable. |
| `--dry-run` |  |  | Prints the restore plan through `backup_restore_flow::planned` and changes no store. |
| `--output json\|text` | enum: json, text |  | Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent. |

## Global options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--db PATH` | text |  | Overrides the store address that `db_target::resolve_target` opens; config and environment decide it when absent. |
| `--backend sqlite\|postgres` | enum: sqlite, postgres |  | Selects the store backend that `db_target::resolve_target` hands to the resolver; config or the address decides it when absent. |
| `--bank BANK` | text |  | Scopes the command to one bank; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and the write scope defaults to `default`. |
| `--actor ACTOR` | text |  | Names the acting identity; `cli_read_args::base_args` passes it to the tool and `auth_cli` reads it for the actor commands. |

## Examples

Print the restore plan for one snapshot.
```
clio backup restore clio-20260910T002640Z-0a1b2c3d --dry-run
```

Restore one snapshot without a typed confirmation.
```
clio backup restore clio-20260910T002640Z-0a1b2c3d --yes
```

Restore a second listed snapshot.
```
clio backup restore clio-20260910T002700Z-1b2c3d4e --yes
```
